newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish ruling Social Democrats slip more in polls.
newsitem.headline: Swedish ruling Social Democrats slip more in polls.

text.p: Sweden's ruling Social Democrats were continuing to lose support in the country's opinion polls while the conservative opposition, the Moderates, was gaining, a poll showed on Friday.
A survey by pollster Temo showed support for the minority Social Democratic government had fallen to 26.5 percent while the Moderates were winning 32 percent of votes.
This was the third consecutive poll to put the Moderates ahead of Prime Minister Goran Persson's Social Democratic party.
Support for the Social Democrats, who will next go to an election in September 1998, is now at its lowest since April 1991.
The poll, published in daily newspaper Dagens Nyheter, said young people, low paid and less educated people, and women had left the party since the last general election in 1994.
Support for the Social Democrats has fallen since January and it seems the fall is related to tough fiscal policies with cutbacks.

The figures did not indicate the decrease stemmed from the government's decision to phase out nuclear power in Sweden. The government agreed with the Centre and Left parties in January to close one reactor next year and another in 2001.
The blue collar trade union umbrella group, LO, was still a strong supporter of the government but even its level of support has slipped, the poll found.
Temo interviewed 1,552 people for the poll.
